_note: How big things should be, and why. The factory reads this file; SIZING.md explains it. Sizes are millimetres and follow from a short list of facts about bodies and everyday objects, so changing one fact (say, finger) moves every part that depends on it. Formulas may use any fact name, + - * /, min() and max(). Edit here, never in code. tools/propkit/sizing.py --catalogue regenerates parts_catalog.json from this file.

finger.why: adult index finger, thickness at the middle joint

fingernail.why: the gap a fingernail can get into

hand_width.why: adult palm breadth across the knuckles

pinch.why: the least side a thumb and finger can grip

clearance.why: room around a hand or object so it doesn't scrape

handle_bar.why: thickness of a grab bar or pull you close a hand round

toe_kick_height.why: height of the space for toes under a counter or appliance

counter_height.why: US kitchen counter, 36 in; ranges and dishwashers match it

reach_height.why: highest comfortable reach without a step

spout.why: how far a dispenser spout hangs into its recess

door_thickness.why: a solid street or apartment door, 1 3/4 in

screw_head.why: a typical exposed screw or rivet head

brick_width.why: US modular brick bed depth, 3 5/8 in

masonry_wall.why: lower Manhattan loft and tenement walls run 300-600 mm

rain_drip.why: how far a drip edge must clear the wall face to shed water

handle.why: a hand closes round it: a finger plus clearance behind the bar, plus the bar itself

where.why: shorter than a palm is wide and no one can grip it: it is trim

hinge.why: an exposed knuckle a few mm proud (period appliances and doors)

where.why: hinges sit on an edge of the door

foot.why: levelling feet and casters lift the body off the floor

where.why: feet stand on the floor at the corners, are no wider than a palm and a half, and a view shows two

kick_plate.why: the plinth or base strip along the bottom of an appliance or cabinet

where.why: runs along most of the width, in the toe zone

knob.why: you pinch its side: at least a pinch deep; 2-6 cm knobs stand out about 60% of their diameter (part_rules.py)

where.why: a knob wider than a palm is a dial plate or trim

key.why: typewriter and keyboard keys stand on stems above the deck

cornice.why: building cornices overhang the wall to shed rain; bigger buildings, bigger cornices

sill.why: the nose of a sill must throw water clear of the wall face

panel.why: a door or drawer front stands a few mm proud of the cabinet face, with a gap all round so it can open

seam.why: the gap round a door or drawer: a fingernail, not a slot

appliance.why: on an appliance, parallel gaps in the toe zone are the kick grille

vent.why: louvres and grilles: shadow, not a hole

slot.why: coin, card and mail slots; a mail slot goes through a door

dispenser.why: a glass must fit under the spout

where.why: tall enough for a glass, between waist and eye height, on the front

recess.why: general pockets, handles cut into a panel, display niches

window.why: window glass sits back in a masonry wall, usually about half its thickness

door_opening.why: street doors sit back in their frames, less deep than windows

pit.why: screw heads, rivets and small holes drawn as dots: shadow only

envelopes._note: Believable overall size per category, [min, max] mm, 1960s-70s New York. Intake and the build warn when an object falls outside.

tv.why: tabletop CRT sets; a console set is 'cabinet'

range_atlas.why: cooktop at counter height; backguard excluded

chair.why: a back rises above the seat

telephone.why: 1960s-70s desk set (push-button or rotary): wedge base, handset on a cradle

assembly_rules: The outer shell (cabinet, body) is one continuous surface: a feature in one view never cuts through the whole object.
A part seen in several views is one part: build it once, from the view that faces it.
Panels that open (doors, drawers, lids) are separate pieces with a gap all round.
Feet and kick plates are one standard base, not one piece per view.

profiles._note: Side profiles by convention, for sheets with no side view (low confidence; the report says so). Points (depth fraction from the front, height fraction from the top), front at the left.

telephone.why: desk sets slope up from a low front to the cradle at the back so the dial or keys face the user
